Q1: N,N-Dimethylformamide exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, inhalation, dermal, eye, organ, and systemic effects. It is also listed as a hazardous air pollutant, a potential endocrine disruptor, and a 'Substitute It Now' chemical, indicating broad concerns regarding its health and environmental impacts.
Q3: N,N-Dimethylformamide is extensively characterized, with 177,000 scientific references—significantly above the median for our dataset. Its precise molecular formula (C3H7NO) and classification as a 'Small Molecule' further confirm it is a well-defined chemical with no data deficient hazard classes.
